answer.rationale: The latency is on the write path during peak settlement traffic, so routing reads to replicas (b5) is unlikely to help — the bottleneck is writes, and rollback (b1) is ruled out by the compliance mandate on the security patch. Failover (b2) addresses regional degradation, but no region-level fault is indicated and a mid-peak traffic shift risks write loss, conflicting with the objective. Adding capacity matches the most directly analogous precedent (b3: provisioning headroom absorbed a heavy write/traffic surge without customer impact) and is reversible without touching the protected release. I verify b3 to confirm it generalizes beyond a pre-planned peak to a live incident, and b2 to check whether failover is actually a better-supported fallback if capacity addition stalls. Uncertainty remains: if the new release introduced a write-path regression rather than pure saturation, added capacity will mask but not fix the climb, so this must be paired with monitoring rather than assumed resolved.
